**Shape.** U27, "compatibility of tolerance bounds", took the synthesis
([CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md)) to the joint satisfiability of demands within tolerances.
U28 pointed at the record's sheaf tools. U29 and U30 asked for more. U31
asked to "connect to individuation". U32 asked what the record should add,
and U33 diagnosed the record as "flush with negative assertions and
distinctions" and asked for positive accounts, even as proposals.

**The diagnosis.** Roughly right for the interpretive layer: a crude title
grep finds a negation in 215 of 376 live thesis claims. But the record's
demonstrated layer is mostly positive characterizations already: [CLAIM-153](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md),

*Reconstructed on 2026-11-04. The source is a ChatGPT share, https://chatgpt.com/share/6aea715b-e488-83ea-8900-c390288262ba, titled "Organizational Nucleation and SLT". It continues "Assess SDT Coverage": its U1 links that exchange's second share, whose U27–U33 were filed on 2026-11-03. It has 29 owner turns, from U1 at about 20:02 UTC on 2026-11-02 to U29 at about 05:35 UTC on 2026-11-03.*

*Seven readers read every turn in full. Each checked every record code the replies cited, redid the mathematics, reran the code where it could, and verified the identifiers of the works named. Each then searched the record again with what the reading surfaced. Codes filed from the exchange carry tmp codes until merge.*

**Gaps in the export.**
- **Two answers are lost.** A11 and A15 show only an opening sentence or paragraph and then "The output of this plugin was redacted". A16 answers U15 point by point. Whether it restates a lost A15 cannot be told.
- **Tool output is redacted throughout.** The replies read the record through a GitHub plugin, so what A actually opened cannot be seen. This affects A2–A3, A6–A10, A13–A14, A16, A19–A20, A25 and A28–A29.
- **The U4 attachments are not in the share.** They are U32–U33 of the earlier exchange, and A4 cites them only by file reference.

**Shape.**
- **U1–U5:** the owner's bridge from recurrent incompatibility to the record's singular learning theory account. The owner corrected A twice, at U2 ("nucleation" is the inquiry) and U5 (one object, not two).
- **U6–U7:** niche differentiation, and the owner's correction of "competition" to frustration.
- **U8–U11:** new CASE constructions, resource-bounded legibility and tolerance, normative axes, and tolerance as endorsement.
- **U12–U16:** the owner's directed tolerances, liking against wanting, Frankfurt's sense, the owner's perspectives model with intervention thresholds, and the crowd cases.
- **U17–U21:** the owner's activation threshold, the U18 correction, the U19 chain, and a plan for figures.
- **U22–U25:** the complex and the will drawn, and the owner's turn to a sheaf.
- **U26–U29:** a synthesis, a simulation, motivating perspectives, and maladaptation.

**What the replies did well.**
- **Concessions.** They took the owner's corrections at once and in substance:
  - A2: "I treated “nucleation” as the physical mechanism rather than the name of the research project".
  - A5: "your objection is right, and my distinction was too sharp".
  - A18: "I made activation depend on instrumental rationality".
- **Cited codes.** These were described correctly nearly everywhere.
- **Hedges.** "stipulated", "illustrative" and "not established" stayed visible to the end.
- **Mathematics.** It held wherever it was checked, with three exceptions:
  - A4's ∀∃ ⇏ ∃∀ needs [CLAIM-535](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md)'s restriction to policies acting on observations;
  - A23's inline SVG draws g_i ≥ 0.6, not 0.4;
  - A25's first script was a SyntaxError.
- **A27's simulation.** It reproduces exactly.

**What they did badly.** The record's usual weakness: held results announced as new.
- **The sheaf account U3 pointed to.** U3 pointed A at [CLAIM-538](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) and [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md), and no reply ever cited them:
  - A9 restated [CLAIM-538](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md)'s cycle certificate as "a particularly elegant consequence";

- **The turns the owner supplied at U4.** [CLAIM-535](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md), [CLAIM-534](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) and [CLAIM-532](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) were filed from them, and A4 cited none.
- **The record's own toy models.** [CASE-191](../../record/cases.d/CASE-191.md) (self-formation driven by frustration), [CASE-153](../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md) (the sentry), [CASE-119](../../record/cases.d/CASE-119.md) (the hollow triangle), [CASE-129](../../record/cases.d/CASE-129.md) (the two quiet alarms) and [CLAIM-446](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md) (governance-maintained anxiety) were each re-derived without citation, [CASE-153](../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md) three times.
- **A20's "key mathematical gap".** This is [CLAIM-349](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s ordinal form and [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md)'s last clause.
- **Psychological flexibility.** A defined it by redefining the term. The result is [CLAIM-349](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s organizational flexibility, not ACT's sense ([LIT-555](../../record/literature.d/LIT-555.md), [THEORY-050](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-050.md)).

## Two findings worth keeping

- **[CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md)'s "lacks" clause.** The soliton readings report Kerr solitons with an existence window and path dependence under a pump that does not depend on the soliton. Read with Herr et al. ([NOTE-1692](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1692.md)), the soliton's uptake of the pump is parametric and drawn through its own field, so the Kerr case is [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md)'s state-dependent uptake from a fixed flux, not supplied repair. The clause was kept, scoped to repair supplied at a rate set by the supply alone. [CLAIM-606](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) has a note saying its qualification of [CLAIM-604](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) now rests on the oscillon.
- **[THEORY-1483](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1483.md)'s stability.** A reconstruction of Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's model from the equations the reading quotes (scratch/formal/azam_stability_check.py) reproduces the steady states, the saddle at the low-aid point and the myopic threshold, but finds the high-aid point an unstable focus with no stable manifold, so not saddle-path stable. The paper's system may differ from the reconstruction. The reading stays Proposed; [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) and [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) cite that stability in prose and should be revisited if the doubt holds.

## About the worklist

A history note that names an objection counts, for the worklist, as the whole objection written in, even when only part of it was conceded. That is how [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) showed as ready. A reviewer caught it by reading the defeater; the script does not.

## About the worklist

- Version 8 worked as meant. Its new section listed four demonstrated claims grounded on readings. Two came free by moving an edge, and two by reading the source. The section is now empty.
- Two patterns surfaced for a later check:
  - a promote_when that asks a title's declared-open clause to be decided;
  - a defeated_if whose wording goes stale once a work it calls unread is read ([CLAIM-533](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md)'s still says the record "has not read" Kane's reply).
- Reviewers' version bumps for a dated note alone were not uniform. Cluster S bumped and the others did not. The proposal in dmarx/nucleation#416 would settle what a note takes.

## About the sweep

- A title that reports what a source finds was most often wrong by dropping a hedge, not by inventing a result. Twenty of the 63 promotions needed a narrowing first.
- Many readings filed on 2026-11-05 and 06 carried promote_when conditions that asked for replication. [ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) moves those off the reading. Gathering them by topic, as T1 did, keeps the QUESTION list readable.
- Reviewers again differed on whether a dated note alone takes a version bump; dmarx/nucleation#416 would settle it.
